name: S. 1. inconspicuus
description: Single white to pale blue, throat sometimes blue-purple, 1-6 per peduncle, petals curve backward. Leaves small, oval, pale green beneath, edges slightly wavy, upper surface hairless except on edges. Miniature trailer. Earlier description: Single small blue-spotted white, atypical of other species, one or more per peduncle. Frail. Not known in collections. Miniature trailer.
notes: Formerly listed as: S. 1. inconspicua; S. inconspicua. Names and descriptions follow K. Barbi, African Violet Species Identification Guide (MAAVS memo addendum, January 2019), which uses the accession list of J. Smith and W. Goretsky, Gesneriads 68(1), 2018. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

name: S. 2. afroviola
description: Single white with bluish edges, 1-4 per peduncle, slightly bell-shaped. Leaves small, elongated ovals, purple beneath, edges smooth, upper surface with sparse long hairs, edges with shorter denser hairs. Miniature rosette to slightly trailing. Earlier description: Single, tiny white /mauve top petals, one or more per peduncle. Leaves tiny, triangular/purple back. Not known in collections, but may exist in some mountain ranges in Tanzania. Miniature.
notes: Formerly listed as: S. 2. pusilla; S. pusilla. Names and descriptions follow K. Barbi, African Violet Species Identification Guide (MAAVS memo addendum, January 2019), which uses the accession list of J. Smith and W. Goretsky, Gesneriads 68(1), 2018. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

name: S. 3. shumensis
description: Single pale lilac to nearly white with darker purple spot towards base of the upper petals, 1-4 per peduncle, rarely 6. Leaves nearly round, white to pale green beneath, edges toothed, upper surface shiny with sparse long hairs on raised bumps. Miniature to semiminiature rosette, but may form multiple crowns. 1963 Master List: Midget type. Multiple crown, rather flat growth, with small, almost round, slightly serrated leaves: Short petioles and almost white flowers.
notes: Formerly listed as: S. shumensis. Names and descriptions follow K. Barbi, African Violet Species Identification Guide (MAAVS memo addendum, January 2019), which uses the accession list of J. Smith and W. Goretsky, Gesneriads 68(1), 2018. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

name: S. 3. cl. shumensis
description: Original description (B. Burtt, 1955): Single pale blue to almost white/variable darker eye, usually four per peduncle, sparse bloom. Bright green, pebbled, glossy, slightly serrated, short petiole, leaf blade twisted in some clones. Single crown, but tends to sucker easily. Miniature to Semi-miniature.
notes: Clone of S. shumensis. Described by B. Burtt, 1955. Formerly listed as: S. shumensis. Names and descriptions follow K. Barbi, African Violet Species Identification Guide (MAAVS memo addendum, January 2019), which uses the accession list of J. Smith and W. Goretsky, Gesneriads 68(1), 2018. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

name: S. 3. cl. shumensis Mather EE
description: The difference between the two clones is size: Mather EE looks much the same as S. 3. cl. shumensis but is 2-3 times larger in both leaf and plant size. Flowers are only about 25-50% larger. Dr. Jeff Smith has long suspected that Mather EE may be a tetraploid of the regular clone; since he has not checked the chromosome number, he has been reluctant to label it an "Amazon" clone. Both clones have strawberry pebbling on the leaf surfaces with long hairs at scattered intervals, and both tend to set seed pods spontaneously. The flower color is always a light blue, varying slightly with growing conditions.
notes: Clone of S. shumensis. Names and descriptions follow K. Barbi, African Violet Species Identification Guide (MAAVS memo addendum, January 2019), which uses the accession list of J. Smith and W. Goretsky, Gesneriads 68(1), 2018. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

name: S. 4. teitensis
description: Single purple, 3-4 per peduncle, hairs on back of petals. Leaves variable, but usually longer than wide, dark green and shiny above, pale green to purple beneath, edges shallowly toothed, petiole attaches to blade from underneath rather than on end in mature leaves, upper surface with dense hairs.Standard rosette. Original description (B. Burtt, 1958): Single light blue-violet; 1-2 per peduncle, rare blooms hide under leaves. Dark, slightly pointed, may spoon; thick, rough, brittle, glossy/red, sometimes light green back. Usually grows upright. Standard.
notes: Described by B. Burtt, 1958. Formerly listed as: S. teitensis. Names and descriptions follow K. Barbi, African Violet Species Identification Guide (MAAVS memo addendum, January 2019), which uses the accession list of J. Smith and W. Goretsky, Gesneriads 68(1), 2018. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
